== Biography ==
{{African-American Sticker}}
Rachel Glasgow was born in 1842 in Pennsylvania. She was the daughter of [[Brom-40|Mary]] and [[Glasgow-752|Robert Glasgow]], and the younger sister of Civil War veteran [[Glasgow-751|London Glasgow]] of the 54th Massachusetts Volunteer Infantry, the first regiment in the United States made up entirely of enlisted men of color. Her brother London was missing in action and presumed killed in action at the Second Battle of Fort Wagner in 1863.

She married Civil War veteran Robert Saulsbury who served with the 127th United States Colored Troops (USCT.)

===Occupations===
* 1870, 1880: Keeping house

===Residences===
* 1880: West Marlborough, Pennsylvania with her husband and children
* 1870: Highland, Pennsylvania with her husband and children
* 1850: West Marlborough, Pennsylvania with her parents and siblings

===Death===
She passed away in 1926 and is buried at Union Hill Cemetery in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania.
